title: Energy-Aware Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization with Depletion Safety Constraints for Multi-Robot Coordination

stated_gaps.text: Prior MARL optimizes task performance without explicit resource (energy) consideration, causing depletion risk
stated_gaps.quote: The existing multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches optimize for task performance without explicit energy consideration, leading to inefficient consumption and depletion risk.

stated_gaps.text: Energy consumption is predictable from own actions (R2=0.89); no uncertain, environment-estimate-dependent depletion like dose from an unknown source, and no risk sharing between agents with unequal budgets

thesis_relevance: Closest analogue: per-robot non-renewable budget handled by predictive action masking in MAPPO; the thesis extends this to a budget whose consumption depends on an uncertain particle-filter estimate.

title: Provably Safe Reinforcement Learning: Conceptual Analysis, Survey, and Benchmarking

stated_gaps.text: Most safe RL gives no hard guarantee; methods are unsafe early in training
stated_gaps.quote: Thus, these methods can be unsafe during training, especially initially, but usually converge to a safer policy without formal safety guarantees after sufficiently many training steps.

stated_gaps.text: Assumes full observability and stationary dynamics
stated_gaps.quote: Hereby, we assume that the set of states S is fully observable with bounded precision.

stated_gaps.text: Masking that verifies only few actions blocks exploration and learning
stated_gaps.quote: If η(s) can only verify one or a few actions efficiently, the agent cannot learn properly because the agent cannot explore different actions and find the optimal one among them.

stated_gaps.text: Agents may learn to be safe but ignore the task (goal misgeneralization)
stated_gaps.quote: Third, the agent might learn to perform actions safely but ignore the task objective due to goal misgeneralization (Langosco et al., 2022).

stated_gaps.text: Reduce conservativeness of safe action sets; automate engineering decisions
stated_gaps.quote: Future research could mitigate this through modular and automatic approaches, where fewer engineering decisions are necessary and more parameters are tuned automatically.

stated_gaps.text: Multi-agent: violations caused by other agents are excluded from the definition
stated_gaps.quote: Hereby, inevitable safety violations caused by other agents are not considered to be the fault of the agent and are, therefore, not considered unsafe.

thesis_relevance: Directly frames the thesis safety layer as action masking; the full-observability assumption is exactly what the thesis breaks (safety verified on an uncertain particle belief).

title: SAUTE RL: Almost Surely Safe Reinforcement Learning Using State Augmentation

stated_gaps.text: State grows with number of constraints; scalability
stated_gaps.quote: Therefore, the dimension of value functions and policy grows and potentially can lead to scalability issues.

stated_gaps.text: Does not prevent violations during training
stated_gaps.quote: Sauté RL does not currently address the problem of constraint violation during training, which is still a major problem in safe RL.

stated_gaps.text: Probability-one constraints can be too restrictive
stated_gaps.quote: The constraint satisfaction almost surely is a very strong criterion and in some applications, it can be too restrictive.

stated_gaps.text: Evaluate augmentation on CVaR / average constraints and model-based RL
stated_gaps.quote: Furthermore, it would be interesting to evaluate the effect of safety state augmentation on average and CVaR constrained problems.

stated_gaps.text: Remaining budget is assumed exactly known; not addressed when future cost depends on an uncertain estimate or in multi-agent settings

thesis_relevance: Supports feeding each robot its remaining dose budget as an observation and sampling budgets per episode (enables unequal-budget training); multi-agent, multiple-budget case is an open gap the thesis touches.

title: Effects of Safety State Augmentation on Safe Exploration

stated_gaps.text: Initial burst of violations is unavoidable for model-free learning

stated_gaps.text: Cannot fix without assumptions about environment

stated_gaps.text: Gains come at sample-efficiency cost
stated_gaps.quote: We achieve this performance and safety boost at the expense of sample efficiency since we effectively learn a series of safe policies.

stated_gaps.text: Disturbance-caused violations and lack of guarantees out of scope

thesis_relevance: Budget curriculum (scheduling the safety budget) is a candidate remedy for MAPPO-Lagrangian timidity; model-error-induced violations they leave out are the thesis's overconfidence finding.

title: Risk-Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Percentile Risk Criteria

stated_gaps.text: Risk-constrained formulations largely unaddressed

stated_gaps.text: VaR not coherent and ignores tail beyond threshold

stated_gaps.text: Importance sampling for tail gradient estimates; robotics applications
stated_gaps.quote: Using importance sampling methods (Bardou et al., 2009; Tamar et al., 2015) to improve gradient estimates in the right-tail of the cost distribution (worst-case events that are observed with low probability)

stated_gaps.text: Choosing risk-aversion parameter is hard

thesis_relevance: The thesis's 97th-percentile-over-particles mask is a VaR-style criterion; this paper argues CVaR is preferable, a cheap ablation the thesis can add.
